summary: Alamance County's first fire tower, 100 ft, built 1959 for Cane Mountain; an unsafe old tower stands atop Cane Creek Mountain; a 2025 observation tower is open.

facts.design: 100-foot tower with a base of about 22 feet square and a small observation house at the top, reached by 133 steps
facts.status_note: Sources describe an abandoned, unsafe fire tower atop Cane Creek Mountain. They do not confirm that it is the 1959 Cane Mountain tower.

access.note: Wikipedia says the fire tower atop Cane Creek Mountain is no longer safe for use; no source describes a formal closure order. A 2025 observation tower on the mountain is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: Do not climb the old fire tower. The 2025 observation tower is reached by the Lookout Trail from Oak Hill Trailhead off Bass Mountain Road.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erected by June 1959 as Alamance County's first fire tower; an August 1958 item had reported it bought and planned for Cane Mountain that summer
Expected to go into full operation in September 1959, once a two-way radio and telephone were installed
First year the tower ran for an entire fire season, per a 1967 clipping
A July 2025 blog describes an abandoned fire tower on the highest point of Cane Creek Mountain; not confirmed as the 1959 tower
New 80-foot steel observation tower opened on a secondary peak of Cane Creek Mountain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1959 item places the tower on Bass' Mountain. Wikipedia and a 2025 blog place the old fire tower on top of Cane Creek Mountain, the range's highest point. No source says whether these are one tower, so the record is left as it is.

notes_for_editor: The 1958-1967 clippings firmly support the 1959 build and early service. Nothing dates the end of the 1959 tower. The only present-day evidence is a July 2025 blog and an undated Wikipedia sentence, so the link between the abandoned tower on Cane Creek Mountain and the Cane Mountain record is unproven. The radio forum thread (radioreference, threads/cane-mountain-alamance-county.481463) returned HTTP 503 and was not read. Check on a map whether the record point (35.94638, -79.43444) sits on Cane Creek Mountain or on Bass Mountain. The access and status values are inferred from a Wikipedia sentence and a blog; a site visit or a Forest Service record would settle them.
